> Sounds possibly related to:
> 

I don't think it's related. In that issue it works on compatibility mode in the desktop and only fails on web. In this case the issue is reproducible on desktop as well. It's not an exclusive issue to web. I just ran their MRP here on desktop and it looks as it should.

I found that if I call `glTexParameterf(target, GL_TEXTURE_LOD_BIAS, texture_mipmap_bias);` in the `Texture` struct `gl_set_filter` method it does set the texture_mipmap_bias and works as expected. (also adding a `texture_mipmap_bias` that I'm added into the `GLES3::Config` and am setting with the `RenderSceneBuffersGLES3` when it's configured)

That however only works when the texture is first being loaded. If I change the texture_mipmap_bias after the fact the only way of that texture behaving correctly is for me to unload/reload it (which I have done to test by loading a different scene, waiting a moment, and loading the test scene.

I think the only part of the puzzle I'm missing now is how to trigger a "forceful" reload or re-setting of the filter on the already loaded textures when the texture_mipmap_bias changes.

Mipmap LOD bias (outside of `textureLod()` in shaders) is only available in desktop OpenGL, not OpenGL ES or WebGL.

As per my comment on the contributors chat, we could in theory implement this for desktop platforms only. However, since Compatibility is often used on mobile and web platforms, this would lead to surprises on export where mipmap LOD bias wouldn't work anymore. Therefore, I'm not sure it's worth implementing.

Vulkan is what makes mipmap LOD bias feasible on mobile platforms (and possibly WebGPU for web, but I didn't check).

To improve texture quality at a distance (e.g. for VR), something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10096 or https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7411 can be made to work in all renderers including Compatibility.

Those are great and I believe they solve my problem :)

I think in my case, in WebXR, the asset is selecting the wrong mipmap for the distance, if compared with the regular nonXR version. Which could be a bug, not sure. But the linked proposals do help with the issue.

I would close the issue, but I think at least in the documentation for the `texture_mipmap_bias` it should mention that it's Forward+ and Mobile only and doesn't do anything in compatibility so people that are reading know what to expect, right?
